Area.evidence_source: High on drugs. I know I will. I say to myself I won't, I say to myself in here every day I'll go out there and stay clean – but I know I won't, I just know I won't. I'll go out, I'll get the train, my missus will be at the train station and she'll go, do you want any gear? Before I've even said hello or given her a hug or anything, the first thing she'll ask me is do you want any gear. (R3); This lack of control can therefore be seen in terms of a restricted agency, which is inextricably caught up in a narrative identity created in the past, with each decision and action being an iteration based on the past. It can potentially also be seen as a fractured reflexive, where negative internal dialogues do not lead to productive action. For James this is extreme, with habitual use of substances before despair has even arisen. He also appears to cede any remaining agency to his missus or female partner. Peter, in contrast, portrays more agency in his desire to escape the present, while also searching for answers.
